names every miss. Deleting the cut outright terminates and

mentl/8369b7c:
Two new prime directives at the very top:
- ⌖ Think in the five verbs — reason/write/design in |> <| >< ~> <~ ALWAYS, in
  thinking and prose, not only in .mn. A generic `->` is an unclassified flow;
  naming the verb is what catches foreign-fluency drift. Holds at every altitude
  (a debug trace is |>, fanned hypotheses are <|, a probe under a context is ~>,
  fix→observe→fix is <~).
- ⟲ The manual self-optimizes — CLAUDE.md folds into itself as Mentl folds into
  its seed: each session's durable meta-lesson folds back (here or a protocol_*),
  stale lines pruned in the same motion, held to .mn source's standard (Anchor 6),
  consolidating toward the tightest cached prefix (MRCR cliff), ratcheting toward
  the anchor as the medium absorbs its own discipline.

The self-optimization directive proved itself immediately: the "eprint_string is
silent in m2" note in ⊚ was STALE (eprint DOES print in mentl2, verified
2026-06-15) — corrected in place, plus two folded-in meta-lessons: PROBE THE
ARTIFACT not the plan's hypothesis (the row-poly was a deeper-masked blocker
found by disassembly, not the plan's named one), and THE TRAP MARCHES (each
root-cause fix moves the trap deeper = progress). Full session arc crystallized
in memory protocol_effect_polymorphism_arc_2026_06_15.

mentl/8328284:
Six improvements to the WASM backend:

1. Shared declarations in wasm_collect: NL/DQ/BS constants, WasmOut and
   ExprEmit effects, ctx accessors, find_param_idx — all moved from
   wasm_emit and wasm_construct to the shared module they both import
2. is_handler_global predicate: extracted duplicated 4-prefix check
   (__hs_, __save_, __ev_op_, __ev_result) into one function
3. Unified emit_bind_fields: deleted identical emit_bind_tuple_fields
   (same memory layout, same WAT output, same recursive structure)
4. Single-match supercollector: collapsed 5 sequential match blocks in
   visit_node into one match returning a 5-tuple. Required fixing
   collect_locals_expr to recurse into LMakeTuple, LMakeList, LCall,
   LMakeVariant, LBinOp, LUnaryOp, LIndex, LStore — a pre-existing
   gap where nested locals were silently dropped
5. Fixed emit_call_expr double emission: computed function expressions
   were emitted twice (unsafe for side effects); now uses local.tee
   with dedicated __call_ptr temp
6. Streaming escape_wat_bytes: O(N) via out() effect instead of O(N²)
   string concatenation for WAT data segment encoding

clob/8369dd3:
Adds src/crystal/synth.rs with a 5-primitive DSL whose compositions are
guaranteed to land in {-1, 0, +1}-valued d×d matrices:
  Identity, Shift(k), Negate, Reverse, Mask(bits)

This is the "ternary-reducible DSL" trick the Plan agent flagged as the
key to keeping E a 2-week phase rather than a PhD thesis: program
equivalence is just matrix equality. `find_program(target, d, depth)`
runs a BFS over primitive sequences up to `depth` ops, materializing
each composition as an i8 matrix and comparing to the target. Depth 4
with ~30 primitives enumerates ~800k candidates and is tractable (14s
for the non-reducible exhaustive case; orders of magnitude less for
matches, which short-circuit).

`try_synthesize(weight, max_depth)` wraps `find_program` and accepts
only programs that encode in fewer bytes than the ternary matrix —
this is the storage MDL gate. Returns None otherwise.

CrystalModule gains `symbolic_hint: Option<Program>` plus helpers
is_symbolic() and symbolic_compression_ratio(). The existing
runtime path (ternary matmul on the weight matrix) is unchanged;
the hint is metadata noting "this matrix is reducible to N ops".
Two open follow-ups it enables:
  - storage: on save, serialize the program instead of the matrix
    and reconstruct at load.
  - runtime: execute the ops directly via the DSL interpreter
    (already implemented in Program::apply()) — faster for large d.
Neither is wired today; the architectural commitment is.

crystallize() and a new crystallize_from_trits() (used in tests and
by future constructor code) both attach the hint automatically. The
engine's stats() line now reports "symbolic=N" so cmd_crystal and
cmd_boot show it without extra plumbing.

Verification:
  - 8 synth-level unit tests: materialization of identity/shift/reverse,
    planted-pattern recovery for shift, negate, and composed
    shift+negate, non-reducibility for arbitrary targets, storage
    compression gate.
  - 2 crystallize-level tests: planted shift yields a hint wit

bits/83c98b6:
The doodle canvas was one bone line at one width with no way to fix a
stroke short of throwing the whole drawing away. It now has four inks,
three widths, and an eraser that takes the line you touch. Its tools sit
in the timeline's slot below the stage, never over the drawing, and the
dock's undo means the last line while you are drawing it — which is what
undo means there.

Doodle ink rides in the recipe as `strokeStyle`, parallel to `strokes`.
A doodle drawn before colours existed has none and keeps its bone line,
so v0 files draw exactly as they did. The two arrays are reset together
through one helper: a stale ink entry would be written into a
strokeStyle whose length no longer matched, and the recipe would refuse
to parse on the next load.

Casting a photo now reports real bytes. MediaPipe reports no progress
while it fetches 11.8MB of wasm and model, so the files are streamed
first, into the HTTP cache where MediaPipe then finds them, and the
fraction is genuine. The cast sheet stays open behind the system picker
so the progress has somewhere to live and a cancelled picker leaves you
where you were.

Casts land somewhere free rather than at dead centre, so a second photo
no longer hides the first and looks like nothing happened.

Toasts stop stacking. A plain message repeated while the same one is
showing restarts its clock instead of queueing behind it; one carrying
an undo or an expiry never collapses, since each owns its own piece of
work. Three is the cap, and the one pushed out still runs its expiry so
nothing it was holding leaks.

Four new walkthrough assertions: drawing tools never cover the drawing,
a doodle can be drawn in colour, rubbing out takes one line and not the
drawing, and two photos do not stack. 36/36 checks pass, 95 unit tests.
